statement.p: A company set aside a certain amount of money in the year 2000. The company spent exactly {\$36{,}000} from that fund each year on perks for its employees. In 2003, there was still {\$618{,}000} left in the fund.

Let x be the number of years since 2000, and let y be the amount of money, in dollars, left in the fund that year. Use a linear equation to model the amount of money left in the fund after so many years.
The linear models slope-intercept equation is .
In the year 2011, there was left in the fund.
In the year , the fund will be empty.

li.p: A lines equation in slope-intercept form looks like y=mx+b, where m is the slope, and y is the y-coordinate of the y-intercept. We have been told that the account decreases by {\$36{,}000} each year, so the slope of the linear model is -36000 (dollars per year).
So now we have that y=-36000x+b. The next step is to find the value of b. One way is to substitute a point into y={-36000x}+b. We use the point (3,618000).
So this lines slope-intercept equation is y={-36000x}+726000.

So in the year 2011, the fund had {\$330{,}000} remaining in it.
